title: FileZilla saved sites and passwords
whyItMatters: FileZilla can save FTP and SFTP logins, including passwords, in sitemanager.xml and recentservers.xml in this folder. A stranger could use them to reach the same servers.
source: FileZilla wiki, FileZilla Client data directory: ~/.config/filezilla on Linux holds sitemanager.xml and recentservers.xml - https://wiki.filezilla-project.org/FileZilla_Client_Data_Directory
notes: Uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set. Saved passwords may be obfuscated rather than encrypted, so they are readable. The Flatpak build uses a sandboxed config folder and is not matched.

cleanup.exportFirst: Use File > Export in FileZilla to save the site list without passwords if you need the host names.
cleanup.signOut: Change the passwords of the FTP and SFTP accounts this machine connected to, because the saved copies keep working after the file is gone.
steps: Change the server account passwords at the hosting provider.
Uninstall FileZilla with your package manager.
Delete the folder named in the plan using the file manager.
cleanup.risk: Removes the saved site list and passwords from this machine. Server accounts keep working until their passwords are changed.
cleanup.source: FileZilla wiki, FileZilla Client data directory: https://wiki.filezilla-project.org/FileZilla_Client_Data_Directory
